item.title: Building Cooperative Frameworks for Subsea Cable Security in the Indo-Pacific
item.description: Modernized, harmonized regulation and market incentives are needed to reduce risks, speed repairs, and strengthen resilience in subsea cables across the Indo-Pacific.

item.title: Fortifying the Guatemala-Taiwan Partnership for Development
item.description: CSIS Americas Program Director Ryan C. Berg and Henry Ziemer analyze options for strengthening Guatemala-Taiwan cooperation on development.

item.title: Jon Alterman in NYT: America and Israel United to Fight Iran. Both Will Pay a Price.
item.description: In The New York Times, Jon Alterman explores the unprecedented joint U.S. and Israeli strikes, and how Washington may be drifting toward Israel’s strategy of repeated strikes with no clear end. What happens when the U.S. trades problem-solving for perpetual war?

item.title: Iran’s Next Move: How to Counter Tehran’s Multidomain Punishment Campaign
item.description: Iran is executing a multidomain punishment campaign across energy, cyber, and maritime systems to coerce the United States and its partners. The challenge is not stopping attacks, but denying Tehran the economic disruption and strategic leverage they are designed to create.

item.title: Redesigning Japan’s Space Security Ecosystem for a Stronger U.S.-Japan Alliance
item.description: As space becomes a foundational domain for the U.S.-Japan alliance, Japan has important opportunities to strengthen its space security ecosystem.

item.title: Demystifying Iranian Cyber Operations in the U.S.-Iran Conflict
item.description: Senior fellow Nikita Shah analyzes why Iran’s cyber operations will provide an incremental, rather than a decisive military edge in its conflict with the United States and Israel.

item.title: What Are the Implications of the Iran Conflict for Japan?
item.description: The Iran conflict will have both direct and indirect effects on Japan’s economic, security, and energy outlook, as well as its geopolitical environment.
